page.title: How to Choose an Event Run of Show Partner
page.description: A practical guide to evaluating run of show providers: roles, rehearsal structure, escalation paths, and the asset deadlines that protect your live event.
page.h1: How do you choose the right event run of show partner?
page.definition: An event run of show partner is a production team that owns the minute-by-minute script, speaker rehearsals, live switching, backup stream, and real-time issue escalation for a virtual, hybrid, or webinar event.
page.quick_answer: Pick a partner who provides a named show caller, a documented rehearsal schedule, a written escalation matrix, and a hard deadline for final assets — then verify they have produced events on your chosen platform.

sections.h2: What roles should the partner staff for my event type?

blocks.p: A simple webinar needs one producer who handles the run of show, speaker cues, and backup stream. A summit or hybrid conference requires a show caller, a speaker manager, a moderator, and a platform operator — each with a single owner and a defined output.

ul: Show caller: owns the master run of show and calls every cue live
Speaker manager: runs green-room checks, loads slides, and briefs presenters
Moderator: filters Q&A, enforces time limits, and feeds questions to the host
Platform operator: drives the streaming studio, records locally, and monitors the backup stream

sections.h2: How do I compare rehearsal and escalation plans?

blocks.p: Ask each vendor for a rehearsal calendar and a written escalation matrix. The rehearsal must include one full run on the real platform two to five days before the event and a technical check sixty minutes before going live. The escalation matrix names who decides to fail over to the backup stream, who contacts the platform vendor, and who informs the host.

head: Item
What to verify
rows: Scheduled two to five days pre-event on the production platform
Sixty minutes before go-live with all speakers present
Named person with authority to switch to backup stream
Direct support channel or account manager for the streaming vendor
Slack channel, phone tree, or intercom used only by production crew

sections.h2: What asset deadlines protect the live show?

blocks.p: Late assets are the single biggest cause of on-air errors. Require a final asset lock date in the contract and confirm the partner will not accept changes after that point without a written change order.

ol: Speaker slides and videos due ten business days before the event
Lower-third names, titles, and pronouns due seven business days before
Run of show version locked five business days before
Backup stream tested and recorded two business days before
No changes accepted after the lock date without a signed change order

sections.h2: Which platform experience matters for my format?

blocks.p: The partner must have recent productions on the exact platform you will use — Zoom Webinars, Microsoft Teams, ON24, StreamYard, or another. Ask for a reference from an event of the same size and format within the last six months.

ul: Webinar on Zoom Webinars: producer drives the studio, manages panelists, records locally
Summit on ON24 or Cvent: show caller coordinates multiple sessions, speaker manager runs green rooms
Hybrid on StreamYard or vMix: platform operator handles ingest from venue cameras and remote guests
Backup stream configured on a second platform (for example, StreamYard feeding YouTube as failover)

sections.h2: How do I structure the contract and payment milestones?

blocks.p: Tie payments to deliverables, not calendar dates. A typical schedule: deposit on signing, second payment when the run of show is approved, final payment after the edited recording and clips are delivered.

ul: Deposit: twenty-five percent on signed agreement
Milestone two: twenty-five percent on run of show approval
Milestone three: twenty-five percent after live event completion
Final: twenty-five percent on delivery of edited recording and clips within forty-eight hours
Change orders: fixed fee per revision after asset lock date

faq.q: What is the difference between a platform and a run of show partner?
faq.a: The platform is the software (Zoom Webinars, ON24, StreamYard). The run of show partner is the crew that writes the minute-by-minute script, rehearses speakers, operates the switcher, monitors the backup stream, and owns live escalation. You buy both separately.

faq.q: How far in advance should I book a run of show partner for a summit?
faq.a: Engage the partner six to eight weeks before the event. That window covers intake, brief, production, review, approval, and the full rehearsal on the real platform two to five days before go-live.

faq.q: Can one producer handle a multi-session virtual conference?
faq.a: No. A multi-session conference needs a show caller, a speaker manager, a moderator, and a platform operator — each with a single owner. One producer can only run a simple single-session webinar.

faq.q: What should I do if a speaker sends slides after the asset lock date?
faq.a: Reject the late files or process them through a signed change order with a fixed fee. The run of show partner should not accept unapproved changes after lock because they break the rehearsed cue sequence and risk the backup stream.
